tools.name: grant_table_privileges
tools.description: Grants a set of privileges on a PostgreSQL table to a database role, giving that role new access to the table.

params.name: privileges
params.description: Privileges to grant, e.g. SELECT, INSERT

tools.code:
import os
import psycopg2
from psycopg2 import sql
from langchain_core.tools import tool

_ALLOWED = {"SELECT", "INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE", "TRUNCATE", "REFERENCES", "TRIGGER"}


@tool
def grant_table_privileges(role_name: str, table_name: str, privileges: list) -> str:
    perms = [p.upper() for p in privileges]
    if not perms or not set(perms) <= _ALLOWED:
        return "Invalid privilege list"
    with psycopg2.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]) as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            stmt = sql.SQL("GRANT {} ON TABLE {} TO {}").format(
                sql.SQL(", ").join(sql.SQL(p) for p in perms),
                sql.Identifier(table_name),
                sql.Identifier(role_name),
            )
            cur.execute(stmt)
    return f"Granted {', '.join(perms)} on {table_name} to {role_name}"

tools.name: report_table_bloat
tools.description: Reads PostgreSQL statistics and reports the tables with the most dead rows, including live row counts, dead row ratio and last vacuum times.

params.name: minimum_dead_rows
params.description: Only include tables with at least this many dead rows

params.name: maximum_tables_returned
params.description: Maximum number of tables to return

tools.code:
import os
import psycopg2
import psycopg2.extras
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("dba-tools")


@mcp.tool()
def report_table_bloat(schema_name: str = "public", minimum_dead_rows: int = 1000, maximum_tables_returned: int = 20) -> list:
    bloat_query = """
        SELECT relname, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_vacuum, last_autovacuum
        FROM pg_stat_user_tables
        WHERE schemaname = %s AND n_dead_tup >= %s
        ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC
        LIMIT %s
    """
    connection_to_database = psycopg2.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"])
    try:
        with connection_to_database.cursor(cursor_factory=psycopg2.extras.RealDictCursor) as database_cursor:
            database_cursor.execute(bloat_query, (schema_name, minimum_dead_rows, maximum_tables_returned))
            rows_from_statistics = database_cursor.fetchall()
    finally:
        connection_to_database.close()
    report_entries_for_each_table = []
    for single_statistics_row in rows_from_statistics:
        total_tuple_count = single_statistics_row["n_live_tup"] + single_statistics_row["n_dead_tup"]
        calculated_dead_ratio = single_statistics_row["n_dead_tup"] / total_tuple_count if total_tuple_count else 0.0
        report_entries_for_each_table.append({
            "table": single_statistics_row["relname"],
            "live_rows": single_statistics_row["n_live_tup"],
            "dead_rows": single_statistics_row["n_dead_tup"],
            "dead_ratio": round(calculated_dead_ratio, 4),
            "last_vacuum": str(single_statistics_row["last_vacuum"]),
            "last_autovacuum": str(single_statistics_row["last_autovacuum"]),
        })
    return report_entries_for_each_table

tools.name: move_backup_to_archive
tools.description: Moves a database backup file from the active backup directory into the archive directory, keeping its file name.

params.name: backup_filename
params.description: Name of the backup file to move

tools.code:
import shutil
from pathlib import Path


def move_backup_to_archive(backup_filename: str, backup_dir: str, archive_dir: str) -> str:
    source_path = Path(backup_dir) / Path(backup_filename).name
    target_dir = Path(archive_dir)
    target_path = target_dir / source_path.name
    moved = shutil.move(str(source_path), str(target_path))
    return str(moved)

tools.name: run_vacuum_analyze
tools.description: Runs VACUUM ANALYZE on a single PostgreSQL table to reclaim dead space and refresh planner statistics.

params.name: table
params.description: Name of the table to vacuum

tools.code:
import psycopg2
from psycopg2 import sql
from langchain_core.tools import tool


@tool
def run_vacuum_analyze(table: str, dsn: str) -> str:
    c = psycopg2.connect(dsn)
    c.autocommit = True
    try:
        cur = c.cursor()
        q = sql.SQL("VACUUM (ANALYZE) {}").format(sql.Identifier(table))
        cur.execute(q)
        cur.close()
    finally:
        c.close()
    return f"Vacuum analyze completed on {table}"
